body:
Another error message that could occur is:

```bash
> helm install ...

Error: release *** failed: *** "services" is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:***:tiller-account" cannot create resource "***" in API group "" at the cluster scope
```

Tiller-Version: 2.9.1
Tiller installed in a seperate namespace.
Provider: Azure AKS

Somehow the tiller cannot deal with the BOM and interchanges namespace, resource etc.
The BOM is meaningless in UTF-8 and is neither required nor recommended. You could fix your tools to not emit nonsense.

It's not just meaningless, it's wrong. UTF-8 is a sparse encoding in the sense that a large fraction of possible byte combinations do not result in valid UTF-8 text. Binary data and text in any other encoding are likely to contain byte sequences that are invalid as UTF-8. Practically the only exceptions to that are when the text consists purely of ASCII-range bytes. Because all modern encodings use ASCII-range bytes to represent ASCII characters, ASCII-only text can be safely interpreted as UTF-8 regardless of what encoding was intended by the system that emitted the bytes. Because of these considerations, heuristic analysis can detect with high confidence whether UTF-8 is in use, without requiring a BOM. Attempting to use a BOM - which has no real significance in UTF-8 (while it does in some other Unicode encodings) - to indicate "This file is UTF-8" is not correct, and is not something other tools should be expected to cope with. It's not simpler than using the heuristic approach, it's just wrong.

Perhaps as you allude it's so common in the Windows world that one has to support it anyway, but that seems absurd. Report bugs in whatever tool you use that is prefacing all your UTF-8 files with a misplaced BOM.

Visual Studio and lots of other windows tools adds this byte mark, and I just wasted 2 hours trying to figure out why with 2 seemingly identical files, one works and one doesn't. 

Not to mention, the yaml files work just fine with kubectl with the BOM, so why can't helm?

It took you 2 hours to work out a single character difference in a pair of
files? If only you'd had a computer handy.

issue.body:
Closes #6081 

Removes the BOM prefix if present, in read files before processing the data.
Affects the following pkg:
- pkg/chart/loader: directory and archive loader
- internal/ignore: when loading .helmignore file

It's my first contribution and I'm no golang expert please be gentle :).

I initially tried another solution with [BOMOverride](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/text@v0.3.2/encoding/unicode?tab=doc#BOMOverride) to also handle UTF-16 BOM but it broke other parts that I did not understand.

Also let me know if I need to backport this to v2.x.
